claims.text: Adding approximately 1 at.% boron to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 will reduce the critical cooling rate required for full amorphization.
Adding approximately 1 at.% boron to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 will increase the crystallization onset temperature of its amorphous state.
The baseline Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy is fully molten and homogenized before quenching.
Phosphorus promotes amorphization of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 during rapid quenching.
Approximately 1 at.% boron will enhance short-range chemical order in the alloy.
Approximately 1 at.% boron will increase connectivity in the local atomic network by forming directional, covalent-like bonds.
Changes in atomic-size and bonding heterogeneity can disrupt crystal nucleation and slow grain growth in multicomponent amorphous alloys.
Boron-induced directional bonding will impede atomic rearrangements needed to form crystal nuclei in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Boron addition will produce a more homogeneously disordered structure that is kinetically trapped in the amorphous state.
Very rapid cooling by melt spinning can produce an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon.
Cooling rate significantly affects the microstructure and phase composition of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The beneficial effect of boron is expected specifically near a concentration of 1 at.%.
Boron concentrations considerably above or below 1 at.% may fail to improve glass formation and amorphous-state stability.
Changes in melt-spinning or rapid-quenching parameters may prevent the anticipated boron-induced improvement.
High configurational entropy favors amorphous-state formation and is correlated with greater glass-forming ability and noncrystalline stability.

contradictions.description: The tests are described as occurring under both ambient atmospheric conditions and an inert environment; these are distinct environmental conditions unless the intended meaning is an inert atmosphere at ambient temperature and pressure.
